issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch in the example program: the template's header declares Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) but the corresponding implementation in Bitmap24.cpp defines Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height) (two parameters). The solution repository uses the two-parameter constructor (int i_width, int i_height). This mismatch in the template is an unintentional structural inconsistency that will cause compilation errors and confuse students about the intended constructor API.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template header match the implementation and the solution: change the constructor declaration in template_repository/example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp to Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height); (remove the extra 'depth' parameter). Alternatively, implement a three-parameter constructor in Bitmap24.cpp that accepts (int i_width, int i_height, int depth) if the extra parameter is intended — but prefer matching the solution (two-parameter constructor) to avoid confusing students.

issues.description: Constructor API mismatch for the Bitmap24 class between template and solution. In the template repository header (example_program/src/Bitmap24.hpp) the class declares a three-parameter constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, int depth) while the template implementation (example_program/src/Bitmap24.cpp) defines a two-parameter constructor Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height). The solution repository consistently uses the two-parameter constructor (Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) in the header and a matching two-parameter definition in the cpp). This discrepancy (extra 'depth' parameter present only in the template header) creates an unintentional API/name/signature inconsistency that will confuse students mapping the header to the implementation and may cause compilation/linking errors or wasted time tracking down why declarations and definitions differ.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template header and implementation consistent with the solution: remove the unused 'depth' parameter from the template header declaration so it matches the implementation (declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height)), or alternatively update the template implementation to provide a matching three-parameter constructor and use the parameter meaningfully. The preferred, minimal fix is to change the template header to declare Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) to match the implementation and the solution API.
